cards.text: It's the eighth day, friend. Aaron and his sons just spent seven days at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting being ordained as priests (Leviticus 8:33-35). Now Moses, Israel's leader, calls in Aaron the priest, Aaron's sons and the elders of Israel.
Moses tells Aaron to take a young bull and a ram for himself and present them before the LORD. My first day in this bakery, my opening act was setting off the smoke alarm. TWICE.

cards.question: Moses gives one rule for both of Aaron's animals, the young bull and the ram. What does each one have to be?
Moses tells Aaron the young bull is for a ___ offering and the ram is for a ___ offering.

cards.text: Then Moses tells Aaron what to say to the Israelites. They need to bring a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb for a burnt offering, an ox and a ram for a peace offering, and a grain offering mixed with oil. Friend, that's not a delivery, that's a whole PARADE.

cards.question: Moses gives Aaron a reason to tell the Israelites for bringing all those offerings today. What is it?

answers.text: Today the LORD will appear to them
Today the camp will set out

cards.text: So they bring everything Moses commanded to the front of the Tent of Meeting. A goat, a calf, a lamb, an ox and a ram. I bet you could hear that walk from the next tribe over.

cards.question: At the Tent of Meeting, only Aaron and the elders come near and stand before the LORD.

cards.text: Moses says, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.” Then he tells Aaron to approach the altar and sacrifice his sin offering and his burnt offering.

cards.question: Moses says Aaron's own sin offering and burnt offering make atonement for Aaron and for the people.

cards.text: So Aaron approaches the altar and slaughters the calf as a sin offering for himself. The whole congregation is watching, so no pressure, Aaron. NO pressure.

cards.question: Aaron's sons bring him the blood of the calf. Where does Aaron put it with his finger?

answers.text: On the horns of the altar

cards.text: He pours out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. Then he burns the fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

cards.question: The calf's fat goes on the altar. Where does Aaron burn up the calf's flesh and hide?

answers.text: At the base of the altar

cards.text: Next comes the burnt offering. His sons bring Aaron the blood, and he splatters it on all sides of the altar.

cards.question: Aaron's sons bring him the burnt offering piece by piece, and he burns the pieces outside the camp.
Aaron washes the burnt offering's entrails and legs before he burns them on the altar.

cards.text: Aaron's own offerings are done. Now he presents the people's offering, starting with the male goat for the people's sin offering.

cards.question: Aaron slaughters the people's goat and offers it for sin the same way as his own sin offering.

cards.text: He offers the people's burnt offering according to the ordinance, then presents the grain offering. A crowd that big, and Aaron STILL sticks to the recipe. I respect a man who sticks to the recipe.

cards.question: Aaron takes a ___ of the people's grain offering and burns it on the altar.

cards.text: Then Aaron slaughters the ox and the ram as the people's peace offering.

cards.question: Aaron's sons bring him the peace offering's blood, and he splatters it on all ___ of the altar.

cards.text: His sons bring the fat portions from the ox and the ram and place them on the breasts. Aaron burns the fat portions on the altar.

cards.question: With the fat burned, what does Aaron do with the breasts and the right thigh of the peace offering?

cards.text: Sin offering, burnt offering, peace offering, all done. Friend, if I finished a list that long, you'd find me asleep in the flour bin.

cards.question: With every offering made, Aaron faces the people. What does he do?

answers.text: Lifts up his hands and blesses them
Sends them back to their tents

cards.text: Then Aaron steps down. He and Moses go into the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: When Moses and Aaron come out of the Tent of Meeting, they bless the people.

cards.text: And then it happens, friend. The glory of the LORD appears to all the people, just like Moses said it would.

cards.question: Fire comes out from the presence of the LORD. What does it consume on the altar?

answers.text: The burnt offering and the fat portions
The breasts and the right thigh

cards.question: When all the people see the fire from the LORD, they shout for joy and fall facedown.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause for now, friend. The priests have only just started their service, and trust me, this story isn't finished.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the instruction, the smoke alarm line and "TWICE." Story cards after the opening card can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the card's core action. The card is about Aaron taking a young bull and a ram to present before the LORD, but the joke is about botching a first day by setting off a smoke alarm. Nothing on the card says Aaron makes a mistake, and the card never says it's his first day. The joke also hints that Aaron's service could go up in smoke, which the passage doesn't support.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question asks about a repeated line. 9:18 repeats 9:12 word for word: "His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar." Stop 1 card 15 already told the baker that Aaron splatters the blood "on all sides of the altar," so this card gives away its own answer, "sides."

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
